full_text:
VISAKHAPATNAM: The Cyclone Akvan intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal on Wednesday morning.
The severe cyclonic storm is crawling towards
Andhra Pradesh and it is likely to cross north Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, by November 20 as a severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100kmph gusting to 110kmph.
The impacts in Andhra Pradesh are very likely to be in the form of extremely heavy rainfall accompanied by strong gales in six coastal districts, heavy to very heavy rainfall accompanied by winds in six districts, and heavy rainfall in four districts.
Authorities in parts of the north coastal Andhra Pradesh have stepped up precautionary measures ahead of the cyclone, they may shift residents of vulnerable and structurally unsafe homes in the region to designated shelters.
Some senior officials were deployed for overall supervision of preparedness, relief and restoration measures.
Cyclone Akvan is likely to make landfall between Narsapur and Puri on November 20, packing wind speeds of 90-100kmph
The cyclone Akvan over westcentral and adjoining central parts of south Bay of Bengal was moving north-northwestwards at slow speed and it lay centred over the same region about 520km southeast of Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh), 560km east of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 570km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 660km south of Gopalpur (Odisha) and 720km south of Puri (Odisha).
The slow speed gives the system time to gain momentum over warm water.
IMD on Wednesday morning forecast that the cyclone would cross land between Nellore and Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh.
It altered the forecast in the afternoon, saying the landfall would be between Narsapur and Puri.
The weather agency expects Akvan to cross the north Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and south Odisha coasts on Friday (November 20) noon. The crossing point is likely to be between Narsapur and Puri as a severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100kmph gusting to 110kmph.
The intensity forecast has been brought down a notch. Initially IMD predicted that the system may landfall as a very severe cyclonic storm, but now expects the landfall as a severe cyclonic storm, not the very severe storm it projected earlier.
Winds of 90-100kmph, gusting up to 110kmph, are expected from Thursday (November 19) night until landfall on Friday, November 20, noon.
Heavy To Extremely Rains
The IMD has issued a red alert (extremely heavy rainfall prediction) for six districts- Kakinada, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR), and Ankapalle and Yanam of Union Territory of Puducherry for Thursday (November 19).
It has issued an orange alert (heavy to very heavy rainfall) for Parvathipuram Manyam, West Godavari, East Godavari and Konaseema districts for Thursday.
Heavy rainfall is likely at one or two places over Eluru, Krishna, Guntur, and Bapatla districts on Thursday. Gale winds speed reaching 90-100kmph gusting up to 110kmph likely at isolated places Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam.
Six districts Kakinada, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Ankapalle and Parvathipuram Manyam and Yanam are covered by the red alert for Friday (November 20), and orange alert for ASR and Konaseema districts, and isolated heavy rainfall over Eluru, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, East Godavari, and West Godavari districts for the same day as well.
Gale winds speed reaching 90-100kmph gusting up to 110kmph likely at isolated places Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam.
IMD has forecast isolated heavy rainfall over Kakinada, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, ASR, Anakapalle, and Manyam districts on Saturday (November 21).

title: Cyclone Akvan Puts Six Andhra Districts on Red Alert - Urban Acres

full_text:
Cyclone Akvan intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal on Wednesday, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting landfall between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha around noon on November 20.
The storm is expected to cross the north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts as a severe cyclonic storm, with maximum sustained winds of 90-100 kmph and gusts reaching 110 kmph. Gale-force winds are forecast from Thursday night through the expected landfall period on Friday.
The IMD has issued a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall in Kakinada, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalle and Yanam for Thursday. An orange alert has been issued for Parvathipuram Manyam, West Godavari, East Godavari and Konaseema. Heavy rainfall is also expected in parts of Eluru, Krishna, Guntur and Bapatla districts.
For Friday, the red alert covers Kakinada, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalle, Parvathipuram Manyam and Yanam. The IMD has issued an orange alert for Alluri Sitharama Raju and Konaseema, while isolated heavy rain is forecast in Eluru, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, East Godavari and West Godavari.
The cyclone was located about 520 km southeast of Narsapur, 570 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam and 660 km south of Gopalpur when the report was published. It was moving north-northwestwards at a slow speed over warm waters.
The IMD revised its forecast on Wednesday. It had initially indicated a possible landfall between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, but later shifted the projected crossing zone to between Narsapur and Puri. The agency also lowered its intensity estimate from a possible very severe cyclonic storm to a severe cyclonic storm at landfall.
Authorities in parts of north coastal Andhra Pradesh have stepped up precautionary measures. Officials may move residents from vulnerable or structurally unsafe homes to designated shelters, while senior officers have been deployed to supervise preparedness, relief and restoration operations.
The IMD has forecast isolated heavy rainfall in Kakinada, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalle and Parvathipuram Manyam on Saturday, November 21.

title: Cyclone Akvan: Red alert in 7 Andhra Pradesh districts, landfall expected on November 20; Odisha, Telangana, Tamil Nadu brace for heavy rain - News24Online

full_text:
Cyclone Akvan is gaining strength over the Bay of Bengal and is expected to reach the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 20. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the storm may bring heavy rain, strong winds, and flooding to coastal areas.
Andhra Pradesh is expected to face the biggest impact, while Odisha, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and other states may also experience heavy rainfall over the next few days.
Red alert issued in 7 Andhra Pradesh districts
Seven districts in Andhra Pradesh have been placed under a red alert for November 19 and 20, according to the forecast. These include Kakinada, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna and Bapatla.
These districts may receive extremely heavy rainfall and experience strong winds as Cyclone Akvan approaches the coast. Other districts, including Visakhapatnam, Anakapalle, Vizianagaram, Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore, are also expected to experience adverse weather conditions.
Residents in coastal and low-lying areas have been advised to remain alert and follow instructions issued by local authorities.
Cyclone Akvan landfall expected on November 20: Which areas are at risk?
Cyclone Akvan is expected to reach the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 20. The storm may make landfall along the central or northern parts of the state’s coastline. However, the exact location is yet to be confirmed and may change as the cyclone moves closer.
The cyclone is also expected to become stronger before reaching the coast and may turn into a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm.
Odisha, Telangana, Tamil Nadu among states on alert
Apart from Andhra Pradesh, several other states are likely to experience heavy rainfall due to Cyclone Akvan and its associated weather system.
In Odisha, heavy to very heavy rainfall is expected in parts of the southern and coastal districts, particularly on November 19 and 20. Telangana may also receive heavy rainfall in isolated eastern districts on November 20 and 21.
Northern Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal may experience heavy rainfall on November 19. Rough sea conditions are also expected along parts of the coast.
West Bengal may receive heavy rainfall in some parts of Gangetic West Bengal on November 19 and 20. Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh could also experience heavy rainfall in isolated areas on November 20 and 21.
Meanwhile, eastern Madhya Pradesh and parts of East Vidarbha in Maharashtra may receive heavy rainfall around November 21. The intensity of rainfall is expected to vary across these states.
Fishermen advised to stay away from sea
With rough sea conditions expected along affected coastal areas, fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. Residents living in coastal and low-lying areas should follow evacuation instructions issued by local authorities.
People have also been advised to keep essential medicines, drinking water, food supplies, flashlights and charged mobile phones ready. Travelling through flooded roads and visiting beaches during severe weather should be avoided.
